---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |

Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. 2. `actionlint`/YAML parse clean; the workflow appears in `gh workflow list`.
3. On the next cart PR, the `detect-changes` job's `e2e_scope` output is literally `cart`, not `skip` and not `full`.
4. With no `@cart`-tagged spec yet present, `e2e-localhost` reports "no tests found" and **passes** — not fails. (`testing.md` documents this as a free no-op.)
5. `e2e_homepage` scoping is unchanged: a homepage-only PR still resolves to `homepage`.

**Skill.** None. Direct edit.

---

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. ### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272

#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)

**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.

**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). **Changes.** Add a Zimmermann-owned `mergeBasket` call at the point `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (around line 230), with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.

`sum_quantities`, not the SDK default `higher_quantity`, because AC5's "combined quantity exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. **This changes every merge, not just over-max ones** — a guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it: today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. It must go in a comment on SFCC-250 (deferred to post-build) because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to know two items is intended.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` asserts `mergeBasket` is called exactly once on passwordless success, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.

3. It asserts the social-IDP route is untouched — no second merge added on top of base `social-login-redirect`'s.

Existing tests for all four still pass, and the PR body names all four as the change's blast radius. This is a shared hook with four call sites and **no CODEOWNERS entry** (see open question 3) — the review that would normally catch a mistake here is not automatically requested.
5. The hook's exported signature is **unchanged**. A signature change would need a team RFC (AGENTS.md "When to Stop").
6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.

#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`

**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.

#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap

**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.

- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library

input.message:
SFCC-315 (ZimmDrawer xLarge width fix, commit 3/18, plan step 1.1) — Overall: PASS, with the Design Fidelity axis explicitly UNVERIFIED, not passed, pending Marcel's own look. Nothing here needs code rework.

## Per-axis table

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | **UNVERIFIED** | No human has looked at the rendered drawer yet. See below — this is a deliberate non-PASS, not a defect. |
| Pass criteria | PASS | All 4 numbered criteria in plan.md's Step 1.1 confirmed with direct evidence, not the report taken on faith (see falsification list). |
| Correctness | PASS | `tsc --noEmit` clean (I ran it myself, exit 0). Targeted `vitest run` on the changed file + `recipeGuards.test.ts` (I ran it myself): 10/10 green. Zero Tester red findings. |
| Conformance | PASS | `zimmDrawer.css.ts:35-36`'s `audit-allow:` comment matches the file's own existing convention (`:61-63`) exactly, and I confirmed by running `npm run audit:tokens` myself that the script actually recognises it. CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`) matches the plan's stated tier — no Tier 1/2 approval skipped. `rem` unit choice is correct per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s Units section (a component width should track root font-size/zoom, unlike the button-height `px` exception). |
| Completeness | PASS | Recipe + its `.css.test.ts` both updated together; component (`index.tsx`) and story already exist and needed no change. |
| Restraint | PASS | `git status` (I ran it myself): exactly the 2 files in the plan's B1 manifest, nothing else. The pre-existing `zimmDrawerShared.ts:12` violation was correctly left unfixed (out of scope, logged not bundled). Tester's extra real-Playwright pass was a single, explained, non-repeated angle on a width/geometry fix — not an over-run. |

## Overall: PASS

Five axes hold on direct evidence, not the Tester's word. Design Fidelity stays UNVERIFIED per this build's own stop-and-ask rule — that's a status, not a failure, and there's no code instruction to give an Implementer here (there's no Implementer in this Light loop, and no defect to send back).

## Answering your four specific questions

**1. Is the fix itself correct/complete?** Yes, on everything I could independently reproduce. I re-derived the arithmetic myself rather than trusting the comment: `128+360+140+430+128 = 1186`, `74.125 × 16 = 1186.0`, `1920 × 0.82 = 1574.4`, `1574 − 1186 = 388` — all four match the code comment exactly. CONFIRMED.

**2. Does the real-browser Playwright measurement change how Design Fidelity should be scored?** No — score it UNVERIFIED, and I'd give you the same answer even if the Tester had measured ten viewports instead of three. Consequence: a wrong visual call here is invisible to every gate that ran (tsc/vitest/audit:tokens all passed on this diff) — that's the whole reason this axis exists as a separate, non-inferred check, per the footer-defect precedent already in my brief. Mechanism: the Tester's measurement proves the *number* (1186px, clamps below that) is real and rendered — that's genuinely strong, better than anything CI runs today — but it doesn't prove *fit*: does 1186px flush-right actually look right against the Figma comp's shadow/border/content padding, does the clamped-at-1000px state look reasonable rather than cramped. That's a different question than "does the width resolve correctly," and it's the one a human glance answers that a width assertion can't. If I let an unusually rigorous automated proxy earn a pass on a categorical human-look rule, the rule stops being categorical the next time someone's proxy looks almost-as-good. Fix: the check the Tester already did means Marcel's look can be quick — confirm `Elements/ZimmDrawer → XLarge` looks right at 1920/1440/1000px, not re-derive any numbers, since those are already proven.

**3. Do the two extra findings change commit-readiness?** No to both, and I confirmed both directly rather than accepting the report. `drawer-menu/index.tsx:147` calls `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmDrawerMenu')` — a wholly separate recipe key from `ZimmDrawer`, registered separately in `theme/components/index.ts:55` vs `:63`. CONFIRMED: never a ZimmDrawer consumer. `zimmDrawerShared.ts:12`'s `DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT = '2.75rem'` — I ran `audit:tokens` myself and it's one of exactly 3 unacknowledged violations reported, no `provisional`/`pending`/`placeholder`/`audit-allow` text anywhere in its comment block. CONFIRMED as pre-existing and correctly out of scope for this commit — it's a different file this step's own ACs never named.

**4. Is "commit 3 of 18" now resolved, or do you want independent verification too?** I verified it myself rather than resting on your confirmation — `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md:839`: `| 3 | fix(drawer): SFCC-315 correct ZimmDrawer xLarge width | 1.1 |`. CONFIRMED, not PLAUSIBLE — exact commit number, exact step, exact subject line all match this diff. When this actually gets committed, use that literal subject so the plan's own commit ledger stays a trustworthy index later.

## What I tried to falsify

Re-ran the plan's own mandated re-check (`grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app`, broadened to both `.tsx`/`.ts`) myself rather than trust the Tester's count — survived: only the type union (`zimmDrawer/index.tsx:44`), the story (`index.stories.tsx:52`), the recipe file itself, and the new test — zero production consumers. Read the actual `drawer-menu` files line-by-line to check the "never a consumer" claim rather than accept it — survived. Recomputed all four numbers in the fix's justification independently — survived exactly. Ran `tsc --noEmit`, `audit:tokens`, and a targeted `vitest run` myself instead of trusting the report — all three survived with output I read line-by-line (not just exit codes). Read `plan.md`'s actual commit table instead of accepting either the Tester's "couldn't confirm" or your own assertion — survived, exact match. Did *not* attempt to re-falsify the real-browser Playwright measurement — repeating an already-thorough, unchanged-diff check is the anti-pattern this build is explicitly watching for; instead I treated "is automated proof enough" as the policy question it is, answered above.

## What I could not verify

Design Fidelity — did not open the story in a browser myself, deliberately (see above: this axis's bar is a human look, an agent re-running the same measurement doesn't change that, and it'd be redundant re-execution against an unchanged diff regardless). The full 1231/1231 suite is PLAUSIBLE from my seat, not CONFIRMED — I ran the specific file plus `recipeGuards.test.ts` myself (10/10 green) rather than the whole suite, since nothing has changed since the Tester's full run and a width constant in one recipe has no plausible mechanism to touch the other ~1225 tests. The three-viewport Playwright measurement is PLAUSIBLE, well-corroborated (the recipe object I confirmed via my own vitest run must produce exactly that rendering), but not independently reproduced by me.
